actions.rationale: Both issues request the same feature: opt-in fragment-free URL identity in the shared normalizer while keeping default behavior unchanged. Issue #3 frames it as 'section anchors appear twice in JSON export'; issue #4 frames it as 'collapse links that only differ after the hash'. Resolution criteria and constraints are identical in both.

Issue #4 body: 'Need an optional way to save one document entry rather than each section. Existing defaults must stay compatible.'

actions.rationale: Issue #8 reports that https://example.com:443/docs and https://example.com/docs produce two export entries. The current main source of bookmarks/urls.py (sha 13d048b, commit 2026-10-11T16:07:50Z) contains `if port is not None and (parts.scheme, port) not in {("http", 80), ("https", 443)}:` which strips :443 from HTTPS URLs before building the authority string, causing both URLs to normalize to the same value. This is confirmed by direct source reading, not merged history alone.
evidence: current_main bookmarks/urls.py line 17 (sha 13d048b): `if port is not None and (parts.scheme, port) not in {("http", 80), ("https", 443)}:` — port :443 on HTTPS is excluded from the authority and therefore stripped.
current_main file commit_date: 2026-10-11T16:07:50+00:00; resolved_ref: main.
Issue #8 body explicitly requests: 'Investigate whether this is already addressed on main before implementing another fix.'

Merged PR #2 (fix/default-ports, merge_commit e565ba0) description: 'Closes #1. Fix URL identity in the shared normalizer; JSON export and CLI inherit the same behavior.' — default-port canonicalization was the stated goal.
actions.uncertainty: Low: current main source directly and unambiguously confirms the canonicalization. No open PR modifies this code path. Live test-run output is unavailable, so behavioral verification by the maintainer is recommended before closing.
actions.draft: Good news: this appears to be already fixed on `main`. The current normalizer strips the default HTTPS port `:443` before building the authority string (`bookmarks/urls.py` line 17, sha 13d048b). Both `https://example.com:443/docs` and `https://example.com/docs` normalize to the same URL. Please verify by running `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v` locally and confirming no regression, then we can close this issue.
